passages.text: “I loathe my own life; I will express my complaint and speak in the bitterness of my soul.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in his suffering.
He feels deep pain.
He hates his own life.
He decides to speak honestly.
He will share his complaint.
He will speak from the bitterness in his soul.
passages.original: נָֽקְטָ֥ה נַפְשִׁ֗י בְּחַ֫יָּ֥י אֶֽעֶזְבָ֣ה עָלַ֣י שִׂיחִ֑י אֲ֝דַבְּרָה֗ בְּמַ֣ר נַפְשִֽׁי׃

passages.text: I will say to God: Do not condemn me! Let me know why You prosecute me.
passages.sermon: Job speaks to God.\r\nJob says, “God, do not condemn me.\r\nTell me why You bring charges against me.”
passages.original: אֹמַ֣ר אֶל־ אֱ֭לוֹהַּ אַל־ תַּרְשִׁיעֵ֑נִי הֽ֝וֹדִיעֵ֗נִי עַ֣ל מַה־ תְּרִיבֵֽנִי׃

passages.text: Does it please You to oppress me, to reject the work of Your hands and favor the schemes of the wicked?
passages.sermon:
God, You are the Creator.
You made me with Your own hands.
Do You find joy in oppressing me?
Do You reject the work You have made?
Do You show favor to the plans of wicked people?
passages.original: הֲט֤וֹב לְךָ֨׀ כִּֽי־ תַעֲשֹׁ֗ק כִּֽי־ תִ֭מְאַס יְגִ֣יעַ כַּפֶּ֑יךָ וְעַל־ עֲצַ֖ת רְשָׁעִ֣ים הוֹפָֽעְתָּ׃

passages.text: Do You have eyes of flesh? Do You see as man sees?
passages.sermon:
God, You are not like a human.
You do not have eyes made of flesh.
You do not see things the way people see them.
You do not look at the world as a man does.
passages.original: הַעֵינֵ֣י בָשָׂ֣ר לָ֑ךְ אִם־ כִּרְא֖וֹת אֱנ֣וֹשׁ תִּרְאֶֽה׃

passages.text: Are Your days like those of a mortal, or Your years like those of a man, that You should seek my iniquity and search out my sin— though You know that I am not guilty, and there is no deliverance from Your hand?
passages.sermon:
God, You are eternal.
You do not have days like a mortal man.
Your years are not like the years of a human being.
You are not limited by time as people are.
Yet You search for my iniquity.
You look for my sin.
You know that I am not guilty.
No one can rescue me from Your hand.
passages.original: הֲכִימֵ֣י אֱנ֣וֹשׁ יָמֶ֑יךָ אִם־ שְׁ֝נוֹתֶ֗יךָ כִּ֣ימֵי גָֽבֶר׃ כִּֽי־ תְבַקֵּ֥שׁ לַעֲוֺנִ֑י וּ֭לְחַטָּאתִ֥י תִדְרֽוֹשׁ׃ עַֽל־ דַּ֭עְתְּךָ כִּי־ לֹ֣א אֶרְשָׁ֑ע וְאֵ֖ין מִיָּדְךָ֣ מַצִּֽיל׃

passages.text: Your hands shaped me and altogether formed me. Would You now turn and destroy me?
passages.sermon:
God, You have hands that create.
You shaped me.
You formed me completely.
You made every part of me.
Now, You turn against me.
You destroy me.
passages.original: יָדֶ֣יךָ עִ֭צְּבוּנִי וַֽיַּעֲשׂ֑וּנִי יַ֥חַד סָ֝בִ֗יב וַֽתְּבַלְּעֵֽנִי׃

passages.text: Please remember that You molded me like clay. Would You now return me to dust?
passages.sermon:
God, You created me.
You shaped me like a potter shapes clay.
You formed me with care.
You have the power to return me to dust.
You can end my life and bring me back to the earth.
passages.original: זְכָר־ נָ֭א כִּי־ כַחֹ֣מֶר עֲשִׂיתָ֑נִי וְֽאֶל־ עָפָ֥ר תְּשִׁיבֵֽנִי׃

passages.text: Did You not pour me out like milk, and curdle me like cheese?
passages.sermon:
God created Job.
God shaped Job’s body.
God formed Job’s life.
God did this with care and intention.
Job says, “You poured me out like milk.”
Job says, “You curdled me like cheese.”
God made Job’s body from simple beginnings.
God changed Job’s form, as milk changes to cheese.
God’s work was careful and skillful.

passages.text: You clothed me with skin and flesh, and knit me together with bones and sinews.
passages.sermon:
God made me.
God covered me with skin.
God covered me with flesh.
God joined my bones together.
God joined my sinews together.
passages.original: ע֣וֹר וּ֭בָשָׂר תַּלְבִּישֵׁ֑נִי וּֽבַעֲצָמ֥וֹת וְ֝גִידִ֗ים תְּסֹכְכֵֽנִי׃

passages.text: You have granted me life and loving devotion, and Your care has preserved my spirit.
passages.sermon:
God gave me life.
God showed me loving devotion.
God watched over me.
God’s care kept my spirit safe.
passages.original: חַיִּ֣ים וָ֭חֶסֶד עָשִׂ֣יתָ עִמָּדִ֑י וּ֝פְקֻדָּתְךָ֗ שָֽׁמְרָ֥ה רוּחִֽי׃

passages.text: Yet You concealed these things in Your heart, and I know that this was in Your mind: If I sinned, You would take note, and would not acquit me of my iniquity.
passages.sermon:
God, You hid these things deep in Your heart.
I know that this was always in Your mind.
If I sinned, You would notice it.
You would not clear me of my wrongdoing.
passages.original: וְ֭אֵלֶּה צָפַ֣נְתָּ בִלְבָבֶ֑ךָ יָ֝דַ֗עְתִּי כִּי־ זֹ֥את עִמָּֽךְ׃ אִם־ חָטָ֥אתִי וּשְׁמַרְתָּ֑נִי וּ֝מֵעֲוֺנִ֗י לֹ֣א תְנַקֵּֽנִי׃

passages.text: If I am guilty, woe to me! And even if I am righteous, I cannot lift my head. I am full of shame and aware of my affliction.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks to God.
Job suffers greatly.
Job feels deep shame and pain.
Job says, “If I am guilty, I suffer greatly.”
Job says, “If I am righteous, I still cannot lift my head.”
Job feels full of shame.
Job sees his own suffering.
passages.original: אִם־ רָשַׁ֡עְתִּי אַלְלַ֬י לִ֗י וְ֭צָדַקְתִּי לֹא־ אֶשָּׂ֣א רֹאשִׁ֑י שְׂבַ֥ע קָ֝ל֗וֹן וּרְאֵ֥ה עָנְיִֽי׃

passages.text: Should I hold my head high, You would hunt me like a lion, and again display Your power against me.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks to God.
Job feels deep suffering.
Job says, “If I lift my head in pride, You will hunt me.”
Job compares God to a lion.
God hunts Job like a lion hunts its prey.
God shows His power against Job again.
passages.original: וְ֭יִגְאֶה כַּשַּׁ֣חַל תְּצוּדֵ֑נִי וְ֝תָשֹׁ֗ב תִּתְפַּלָּא־ בִֽי׃

passages.text: You produce new witnesses against me and multiply Your anger toward me. Hardships assault me in wave after wave.
passages.sermon:
God, You bring new witnesses against me.
You increase Your anger toward me.
Hardships come against me again and again.
Trouble attacks me in many waves.
passages.original: תְּחַדֵּ֬שׁ עֵדֶ֨יךָ׀ נֶגְדִּ֗י וְתֶ֣רֶב כַּֽ֭עַשְׂךָ עִמָּדִ֑י חֲלִיפ֖וֹת וְצָבָ֣א עִמִּֽי׃

passages.text: Why then did You bring me from the womb? Oh, that I had died, and no eye had seen me!
passages.sermon:
Job speaks to God.
Job feels deep sorrow.
Job asks God, “Why did You bring me out from the womb?”
Job wishes he had died at birth.
Job wishes that no one had ever seen him.
passages.original: וְלָ֣מָּה מֵ֭רֶחֶם הֹצֵאתָ֑נִי אֶ֝גְוַ֗ע וְעַ֣יִן לֹא־ תִרְאֵֽנִי׃

passages.text: If only I had never come to be, but had been carried from the womb to the grave.
passages.sermon:
Job is a man who suffers greatly.
\r\nHe wishes he had never existed.
\r\nHe says, “If only I had never come to be.”
\r\nHe wants to go straight from the womb to the grave.
\r\nHe longs for his life to end before it began.
passages.original: כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא־ הָיִ֣יתִי אֶהְיֶ֑ה מִ֝בֶּ֗טֶן לַקֶּ֥בֶר אוּבָֽל׃

passages.text: Are my days not few? Withdraw from me, that I may have a little comfort, before I go—never to return— to a land of darkness and gloom, to a land of utter darkness, of deep shadow and disorder, where even the light is like darkness.”
passages.sermon:
Job is speaking.
Job is suffering.
Job feels his life is short.
Job says, "Are my days not few?"
Job asks God to leave him alone.
Job wants a little comfort.
Job says, "Let me have a little relief."
Job knows he will soon die.
Job says, "Before I go and do not return."
Job will go to a land of darkness.
This land is full of gloom and deep shadow.
This land has no order.
Even the light there is like darkness.
passages.original: הֲלֹא־ מְעַ֣ט יָמַ֣י יֶחְדָּל יָשִׁית מִ֝מֶּ֗נִּי וְאַבְלִ֥יגָה מְּעָֽט׃ בְּטֶ֣רֶם אֵ֭לֵךְ וְלֹ֣א אָשׁ֑וּב אֶל־ אֶ֖רֶץ חֹ֣שֶׁךְ וְצַלְמָֽוֶת׃ אֶ֤רֶץ עֵיפָ֨תָה׀ כְּמ֥וֹ אֹ֗פֶל צַ֭לְמָוֶת וְלֹ֥א סְדָרִ֗ים וַתֹּ֥פַע כְּמוֹ־ אֹֽפֶל׃פ
